items.headline: Netanyahu's bloc loses majority, coalition talks loom
items.summary: Final Israeli election results confirmed that Benjamin Netanyahu and his allies lost their parliamentary majority, setting up weeks of difficult negotiations among diverse parties. Palestinian citizens of Israel, who have often stayed home, turned out in record numbers.

items.headline: Binance says $6.3 billion hit in breach linked to North Korea
items.summary: The crypto exchange flagged a potential security issue affecting about $6.3 billion. Blockchain intelligence firms linked the apparent hack to North Korea.

items.headline: Justice Department escalates Peltola probe as she denies role
items.summary: Federal grand jury subpoenas were issued as the Justice Department widened its investigation of Mary Peltola's Alaska Senate campaign. Peltola denied knowing about an effort to put a same-named spoiler candidate on the ballot.

items.headline: Early voting surges in Senate battleground states
items.summary: An AP analysis finds early voting running well ahead of the last midterm, with sharp increases in states with competitive Senate races. Millions more Americans have cast ballots ahead of Tuesday's election.

items.headline: Judge opens inquiry into DOJ conduct in golf course case
items.summary: A federal judge ordered a formal inquiry into whether Trump administration officials misled the court about plans for the East Potomac golf course in Washington. The inquiry will examine potential Justice Department misconduct.

items.headline: Aid reaches Ukraine's Oleshky under brief truce
items.summary: A humanitarian mission entered the devastated Russian-held city of Oleshky and began evacuations during a short truce agreed to by Russia and Ukraine. It is the most significant pause in fighting of the war so far.

items.headline: Carney sets goal of EU 'associate' membership for Canada
items.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney set a target for Canada to become the European Union's first associate member. The push comes amid trade tensions with the United States.

items.headline: Oil company profits soar again on war-driven prices
items.summary: Major oil companies reported another quarter of very high earnings. The war in Iran has pushed up crude prices and what drivers pay at the pump.

items.headline: Study: human-driven warming may have halted a new ice age
items.summary: Researchers found evidence that warming from fossil fuel use reversed the advance of a new ice age. Yale Environment 360 reported the findings Friday.

items.headline: Massachusetts weighs repeal of recreational marijuana
items.summary: Ballot Question 8 would make Massachusetts the first state to repeal legal recreational cannabis. It would also dismantle the legal framework for social equity cannabis businesses.

digest.overview:
Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola denied knowing of a plan to put a second Dan Sullivan on the ballot as the Justice Department issued grand jury subpoenas in its probe of her campaign. A federal judge rejected the administration's bid to set aside up to 20,000 California ballots of alleged noncitizens, saying it would wreak havoc on voting. Early voting is running well ahead of the last midterm, with sharp jumps in Senate battleground states. Another judge opened an inquiry into whether officials misled the court in the East Potomac golf course case. Binance said about $6.3 billion was affected in a breach that blockchain analysts tied to North Korea, though President Trump said the U.S. does not yet know who was responsible. DoorDash offered $17 billion for Instacart.

Abroad, final Israeli results left Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc with 53 of 120 seats, opening difficult coalition talks, and police said they found no evidence for Likud's fraud claims. Aid reached the Russian-held Ukrainian town of Oleshky under a brief truce, and the State Department approved a $2.1 billion sale of 500 Patriot missiles to Ukraine. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran seeking a deal to end the U.S.-Iran war as more ships were attacked near the Strait of Hormuz. China said its GJ-21 stealth drone made its first takeoff and landing from an amphibious assault ship, and Japan's Foreign Ministry said a breach may have exposed 3,600 personal records. Activision said it will remove real footage of the 2022 Seoul crowd crush from a Call of Duty game.

home.overview:
Friday's NBA slate handed Houston its first loss, 116–111 at Dallas, while Miami poured in 145 against Indiana and Golden State beat the Lakers 112–95. LeBron James and the 76ers beat the Knicks 98–93 in NBA Cup group play to join Detroit, 110–94 winners in Brooklyn, at 5–1 atop the East, and Memphis is 5–0 in the West. Ja Morant faces at least four weeks out with a hamstring strain. Tonight brings seven games, including Thunder at Rockets. In the NFL, Carolina fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero after Thursday's loss to Green Bay, Lamar Jackson will start Sunday at Buffalo, and Cleveland visits Pittsburgh with the AFC North lead at stake.

Achraf Hakimi's hat-trick powered PSG to a 5–1 win at Le Havre and a two-point Ligue 1 lead over Lille, who edged Lens 1–0. Espanyol won 1–0 at Villarreal and Elversberg beat Mainz 4–1. Saturday headlines with Bayern vs. Dortmund, level on 17 points, and Chelsea vs. Man United, with Arsenal chasing a first league win at Anfield in 14 years. In K League 1, Jeonbuk and Daejeon drew 0–0, and K League 2 leaders Suwon Samsung drew 2–2 at Daegu to move within a point of promotion. In the KBO, Kia beat Samsung 4–2 to force a decisive Game 5 in Daegu on Sunday.
